# Magic MessageGate: full documentation

> README.md and AGENTS.md of strapi-plugin-magic-messagegate in one file.
> Source: https://github.com/Schero94/Magic-MessageGate

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Schero94/Magic-MessageGate/main/pics/icon.png" width="96" height="96" alt="Magic MessageGate icon" /></p>

# Magic MessageGate

**WhatsApp, Telegram and SMS for Strapi 5, with templates, delivery tracking and automatic fallback.**

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/strapi-plugin-magic-messagegate?color=4945ff)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/strapi-plugin-magic-messagegate)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-4945ff)](./LICENSE)
[![Strapi 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/Strapi-5.38%2B-4945ff)](https://strapi.io)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-22.21%2B%20%7C%2024.9%2B-4945ff)](https://nodejs.org)

Send a template from your Strapi code, or from any other service, with one call. MessageGate picks the channel, fills in the variables, sends the message exactly once, follows it from _sent_ to _delivered_ to _read_, and falls back to SMS (or to e-mail through Magic Mail) when WhatsApp can't reach the number. It only uses the official provider APIs, so there is no WhatsApp Web session that can get your number banned.

![Message details with the delivery timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Schero94/Magic-MessageGate/main/pics/message-timeline.png)

## Features

- **Three channels, one API.** WhatsApp through Meta's Cloud API, Telegram through the Bot API, SMS through seven.io or Twilio. No vendor SDKs; each provider is a small HTTPS client.
- **Templates with variables.** An editor with a live preview for WhatsApp, Telegram and SMS (including the SMS part count). WhatsApp templates are submitted to Meta from Strapi, and their approval status updates by itself.
- **Exactly once.** A durable outbox in your database. Each message is sent once, also with several Strapi processes, and the same `idempotencyKey` never sends twice.
- **Delivery and read tracking.** Every message has a timeline: queued → sent → delivered → read, or failed with a reason in plain language.
- **Fallback chain.** WhatsApp → SMS → e-mail (through [Magic Mail](https://github.com/Schero94/Magic-Mail), when installed). A number that isn't on WhatsApp is remembered, so the next message goes straight to SMS.
- **Routing rules.** Choose the channel order per template, tag or country.
- **Consent built in.** Consent per channel, STOP keywords (`STOP`, `STOPP`, `ABMELDEN`, `UNSUBSCRIBE`, editable), GDPR export and erasure per contact.
- **Number check.** A free format check (valid, mobile or landline), plus an optional paid line-type lookup through Twilio with a cache and a monthly budget.
- **Safe retries.** Retries after about 1, 5 and 15 minutes, only when the provider provably did not take the message. When the outcome is unknown, the message becomes _uncertain_ and an admin decides, instead of risking a duplicate.
- **An admin that looks like Strapi.** Built only from the Strapi Design System, in English, German, French, Spanish and Portuguese, light and dark, down to phone width.
- **Ready for several instances.** Tested with 8 processes on one PostgreSQL database (Railway replicas, pm2 cluster mode).

## What the official APIs allow

People often ask for things that WhatsApp, Telegram and SMS providers don't offer. Here is what is possible:

| Question                | WhatsApp (Cloud API)                                                                  | Telegram (Bot API)                   | SMS                        | What MessageGate does                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Does the number exist?  | No check before sending. The first send tells you: error 131026 means not on WhatsApp | Only for people who started your bot | Paid carrier lookups exist | Free format check; optional Twilio line-type lookup (cached, budget-capped); learns "not on WhatsApp" from the first send |
| Is the person online?   | Not available                                                                         | Not available                        | Not available              | Shows the **last activity** instead: last reply, last delivery, last read                                                 |
| Has the person read it? | Yes, a `read` status, unless the recipient turned read receipts off                   | No read receipts for bots            | Delivery receipt only      | A timeline per message and a read rate per template; read rates are a lower bound                                         |

## Quick start

1. Install:

   ```bash
   npm install strapi-plugin-magic-messagegate
   ```

2. Configure the plugin in `config/plugins.js`:

   ```js
   module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
     'magic-messagegate': {
       enabled: true,
       config: {
         encryptionKey: env('MESSAGEGATE_ENCRYPTION_KEY'), // 16+ characters, never change it later
         publicUrl: env('PUBLIC_URL'), // https://cms.example.com, used for webhook URLs
       },
     },
   });
   ```

3. Build and start Strapi, then open **MessageGate** in the admin menu.
4. **Accounts → Connect a channel.** SMS or Telegram are the quickest for a first test; WhatsApp needs a Meta app (see below).
5. **Templates → Create template**, then send it from **Messages → Send message**, or from code:

   ```js
   await strapi
     .plugin('magic-messagegate')
     .service('messages')
     .send({
       to: '+4915123456789',
       template: 'order_shipped',
       language: 'de',
       variables: { first_name: 'Anna', order_id: 'A-10423' },
       idempotencyKey: 'order-shipped-A-10423',
     });
   ```

Requirements: Strapi `^5.38.0`, Node.js `^22.21.0 || >=24.9.0`, PostgreSQL, MySQL 8 or SQLite.

Without `encryptionKey`, MessageGate falls back to `MESSAGEGATE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, then `APP_KEYS`, then `ADMIN_JWT_SECRET`. If the key changes later, stored secrets and phone numbers can no longer be read.

## Connect your channels

### WhatsApp (Meta Cloud API)

What the account owner sets up once at Meta:

1. A **Meta business portfolio** and a **Meta app** with the WhatsApp product. **Business verification** raises your sending limits.
2. A **phone number**: a new number for the API, or your existing **WhatsApp Business App** number. Meta calls the second option _coexistence_: you keep using the app on your phone, and Strapi sends through the API.
3. A payment method in WhatsApp Manager. Meta charges per delivered template message, by category (marketing, utility, authentication); see [Meta's pricing page](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing).

Then, in **Accounts → Connect a channel → WhatsApp**, pick one of two ways:

- **Connect with Meta (Embedded Signup).** Opens Meta's own window. Choose a new number, or choose the WhatsApp Business App and scan the QR code with the app. MessageGate exchanges the code for a token on the server and subscribes your app to the number. Server config:

  ```js
  config: {
    providers: {
      meta: {
        embeddedSignup: {
          appId: env('META_APP_ID'),
          configId: env('META_SIGNUP_CONFIG_ID'),
          appSecret: env('META_APP_SECRET'),
          verifyToken: env('META_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN'), // 16-128 characters: A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -
        },
      },
    },
  },
  ```

  In the Meta app, set the webhook callback URL to `https://<your-cms>/api/magic-messagegate/webhooks/meta/app` with the same verify token, and subscribe to the `messages` and `message_template_status_update` fields.

  Strapi's content security policy blocks Meta's script by default. Allow it in `config/middlewares.js`:

  ```js
  {
    name: 'strapi::security',
    config: {
      contentSecurityPolicy: {
        useDefaults: true,
        directives: {
          'script-src': ["'self'", 'https://connect.facebook.net'],
          'frame-src': ["'self'", 'https://www.facebook.com', 'https://web.facebook.com'],
        },
      },
    },
  },
  ```

  If the Meta window can't load, the wizard says so and offers the manual path.

- **Enter credentials manually.** Paste the access token, phone number ID, WhatsApp Business Account ID and app secret. MessageGate then shows the webhook URL and verify token to copy into the Meta app.

### Telegram

1. Open [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather), create a bot and copy its token.
2. Paste the token in **Accounts → Connect a channel → Telegram**. MessageGate registers the webhook with a secret token.
3. A bot can't message someone by phone number. People link their chat through a one-time link (`https://t.me/<your_bot>?start=…`, valid for 30 minutes) that you create in **Contacts** or from code with `service('telegram').createLink(contactId)`.

### SMS (seven.io or Twilio)

- **seven.io**: API key, signing key for status reports, sender ID.
- **Twilio**: account SID, auth token, and a sender number or messaging service. The same account can run the paid number lookup.

Copy the webhook URL shown for the account into the provider's status settings so delivery receipts arrive.

## Sending messages

### From Strapi code

```js
const messages = strapi.plugin('magic-messagegate').service('messages');

// An order update: WhatsApp first, SMS if the number isn't on WhatsApp.
const { id, status, channel, duplicate } = await messages.send({
  to: '+4915123456789',
  template: 'order_shipped',
  language: 'de',
  variables: { first_name: 'Anna', order_id: 'A-10423' },
  idempotencyKey: 'order-shipped-A-10423',
});

// A login code: an AUTHENTICATION template with transactional: true
// needs no marketing consent, and it is dropped if it can't go out in time.
await messages.send({
  to: '+4915123456789',
  channel: 'sms',
  template: 'login_code',
  variables: { code: '482913' },
  transactional: true,
  notAfter: new Date(Date.now() + 10 * 60_000),
  idempotencyKey: `login-${sessionId}`,
});

const detail = await messages.get(id); // status, timeline, fallbacks
```

**Variables in WhatsApp buttons.** A URL button can end in one variable, for example `https://shop.example/track/{{order_id}}`. Pass only the suffix (`order_id: 'A-10423'`); WhatsApp appends it to the URL Meta approved, so a variable can never point the button at another site. Copy-code buttons take their value from `variables` too (at most 15 characters).

### From another service (Content API)

Create a Strapi API token (Settings → API Tokens) with the MessageGate permissions, then:

```bash
curl -X POST https://cms.example.com/api/magic-messagegate/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STRAPI_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data":{"to":"+4915123456789","template":"order_shipped","language":"de","variables":{"first_name":"Anna","order_id":"A-10423"},"idempotencyKey":"order-shipped-A-10423"}}'
```

| Method | Path                                   | Purpose                                   |
| ------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/magic-messagegate/messages`      | send (202 new, 200 duplicate)             |
| GET    | `/api/magic-messagegate/messages/:id`  | status and timeline                       |
| POST   | `/api/magic-messagegate/consent`       | record or revoke consent                  |
| POST   | `/api/magic-messagegate/telegram-link` | create a Telegram link for a phone number |
| POST   | `/api/magic-messagegate/lookup`        | check a number                            |

The Content API only accepts API tokens. Users-permissions logins are refused, because these routes act on any phone number. Set `contentApi.allowUsersPermissions: true` only if you add your own checks.

The full contract (every field, status, event and error code) is in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md).

### Events

React to deliveries without polling. Payloads carry no phone numbers and no message text:

```js
strapi.eventHub.on('messagegate.message.failed', ({ messageId, channel, code }) => {
  strapi.log.warn(`Message ${messageId} on ${channel} failed: ${code}`);
});
```

Events: `messagegate.message.queued`, `.sent`, `.delivered`, `.read`, `.failed`, `.uncertain`, `.expired`, `.discarded`, `.fallback`, plus `messagegate.contact.opted-out`, `messagegate.contact.unreachable` and `messagegate.template.status-changed`.

## Configuration

`config/plugins.js` holds the infrastructure settings. Business settings are edited in **MessageGate → Settings** and stored in the database.

| Option                                    | Default                   | Description                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `encryptionKey`                           | env fallback (see above)  | Key for secrets and phone numbers at rest                             |
| `publicUrl`                               | `server.url`              | Public base URL used to build webhook URLs                            |
| `defaultCountry`                          | `DE`                      | Country for numbers written without `+`                               |
| `defaultNotAfterHours`                    | `24`                      | Deadline for messages without `notAfter`                              |
| `worker.enabled`                          | `true`                    | Set `false` on a process that should not send (for example web-only)  |
| `worker.intervalMs`                       | `5000`                    | How often each process looks for due messages                         |
| `worker.batchSize` / `worker.concurrency` | `10` / `2`                | Messages per claim / sent in parallel per process                     |
| `worker.leaseMs`                          | `120000`                  | How long a claimed message stays reserved                             |
| `retry.delaysMs`                          | `[60000, 300000, 900000]` | Waits before retries 1 to 3                                           |
| `retry.jitter`                            | `0.2`                     | Random spread of the waits (±20 %)                                    |
| `contentApi.allowUsersPermissions`        | `false`                   | Let users-permissions logins call the Content API                     |
| `rateLimits.sendPerMinute`                | `120`                     | Content API sends per API token, shared by all processes              |
| `rateLimits.lookupPerMinute`              | `30`                      | Content API lookups per caller                                        |
| `rateLimits.webhookPerMinute`             | `1200`                    | Webhook requests per account                                          |
| `rateLimits.adminWritePerMinute`          | `60`                      | Admin write actions per admin user                                    |
| `providers.meta.graphVersion`             | built in                  | Pin a Graph API version, for example `v23.0`                          |
| `providers.meta.embeddedSignup`           | none                      | `appId`, `configId`, `appSecret`, `verifyToken` for Connect with Meta |
| `providers.<name>.timeoutMs`              | built in                  | Request timeout per provider (100 to 60000)                           |

**Settings page** (defaults in brackets): default country (DE), consent required (on), opt-out keywords, default channel chain (WhatsApp → SMS), up to 50 routing rules by template, tag or country, e-mail fallback through Magic Mail (off), paid lookup (off, 30-day cache, 500 per month), retention (messages 90 days, webhook receipts 7 days).

## Permissions

Settings → Administration Panel → Roles → Plugins → Magic MessageGate:

| Permission               | Allows                                                    |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accounts: read / manage  | see accounts / connect, edit, test and delete them        |
| Templates: read / manage | see and preview templates / create, edit and delete them  |
| Templates: submit        | send WhatsApp templates to Meta for approval              |
| Messages: read / send    | see messages and timelines / send from the admin          |
| Messages: manage         | retry, discard, mark as sent                              |
| Contacts: read           | see contacts, run the free number check                   |
| Contacts: manage         | change consent, link Telegram, erase, run the paid lookup |
| Contacts: export         | GDPR export of a contact                                  |
| Analytics: read          | see analytics                                             |
| Settings: read / update  | see / change the settings                                 |

For the Content API, tick the MessageGate actions on the API token.

## Consent and privacy

- Sending needs granted consent for the channel. The exception is an `AUTHENTICATION` template sent with `transactional: true` (login codes).
- An opt-out keyword in an incoming WhatsApp, SMS or Telegram message revokes consent for that channel right away, for every process.
- Phone numbers and Telegram chat IDs are stored encrypted and looked up by a keyed hash. Logs only show a short hash prefix, events show none.
- Messages and their events are deleted after the retention period.
- **Contacts → Export** returns everything stored about one person; **Erase** deletes it.
- `metadata` and `tags` are stored in plain text. Don't put personal data there.

## Security

- Every admin route needs an admin session and a MessageGate permission. The Content API needs an API token.
- Provider secrets are encrypted and never returned by the API; the admin only shows whether a secret is set.
- Webhooks use an unguessable URL per account plus the provider's signature: Meta `X-Hub-Signature-256`, the Telegram secret token, the seven.io signature with timestamp and nonce, the Twilio signature. Repeated deliveries are ignored. Failures answer `401` without detail.
- Template variables are plain text with length limits; control characters are removed and Telegram HTML is escaped.
- MessageGate never fetches a URL from user input. Provider addresses are fixed.
- Request bodies, variables (50 per message), metadata keys (20), page sizes and search terms are bounded. Rate limits are counted in the database, so they hold across processes.
- Two runtime dependencies: `zod` and `libphonenumber-js`.

Please report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/Schero94/Magic-MessageGate/security/advisories/new).

## Running several instances

MessageGate keeps its state in the database, so any number of Strapi processes can share it (Railway replicas, pm2 cluster mode, Kubernetes):

- The outbox claims messages with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on PostgreSQL and MySQL 8, and with a conditional update on SQLite, so each message is sent by exactly one process.
- Rate limits, the lookup budget, webhook de-duplication and maintenance jobs use shared database rows.
- Webhooks can reach any process. No sticky sessions are needed.

The test: 8 processes on one PostgreSQL database behind a round-robin balancer sent 500 messages with 0 duplicates. Status webhooks sent in random order to random processes all ended as `read`, and a STOP received by one process blocked the next send on another ([record](./docs/acceptance/2026-11-11-cluster.md)).

Strapi creates and changes database tables at startup. For the first deploy, and for updates that change tables, start **one** replica first, then scale up.

## Costs

MessageGate is free (MIT). The providers charge you: Meta per delivered WhatsApp template message ([pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing)), seven.io or Twilio per SMS, and Twilio per paid lookup ([Lookup pricing](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/user-authentication-identity/pricing/lookup)). Lookups are cached for 30 days, and the monthly budget stops them when it is used up. Telegram is free.

## FAQ

**Can MessageGate check whether a number has WhatsApp before sending?**
No. Meta's Cloud API has no such check. MessageGate learns it from the first send and falls back to SMS.

**Why is a message "uncertain"?**
The request reached the provider, but no clear answer came back in time. The provider may or may not have the message, so sending again could deliver it twice. An admin can retry it (after confirming the risk) or mark it as sent.

**Can I send free text on WhatsApp?**
Only within 24 hours after the contact last wrote to you. Outside that window, Meta requires an approved template.

**Do I need Magic Mail?**
No. It is only used for the optional e-mail step of the fallback chain.

**Can I connect my personal WhatsApp number?**
No. Only a WhatsApp Business App number (coexistence) or a new number can be connected through the official API.

## Migrating from Magic WhatsApp

`strapi-plugin-magic-whatsapp` drove WhatsApp Web through the unofficial `baileys` library and a QR session. That breaks WhatsApp's terms and puts numbers at risk of a ban, so it is gone. MessageGate is a new plugin (`magic-messagegate`) with new routes, permissions and tables; the old package was never published to npm. To move over:

1. Remove the old plugin from `package.json` and `config/plugins.js`, and delete its `.whatsapp-auth` folder.
2. Install MessageGate and connect your number through Meta (the Business App number works through coexistence).
3. Recreate your templates and submit the WhatsApp ones to Meta.

Details are in the [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md).

# AGENTS.md: Magic MessageGate API contract

This file is for AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …) and developers who integrate with `strapi-plugin-magic-messagegate`. It is the exact contract of version 1.x. Everything here matches the code in `server/src`; when in doubt, the code wins and this file is a bug.

Plugin id: `magic-messagegate`. Channels: `whatsapp` (Meta WhatsApp Cloud API), `telegram` (Bot API), `sms` (seven.io or Twilio).

## Rules for agents

Do:

- Send through `strapi.plugin('magic-messagegate').service('messages').send(...)` on the server, or `POST /api/magic-messagegate/messages` with a Strapi **API token** from another service.
- Pass an `idempotencyKey` for every send that may be retried by your code (order id, event id). A second call with the same key returns the first message with `duplicate: true` and sends nothing.
- Pass `notAfter` for anything time-bound (login codes, appointment reminders). A message is never sent after it, not even by an admin retry.
- Use approved WhatsApp templates for business-initiated messages. Free text (`text`) only works inside the 24-hour window after the contact's last WhatsApp message.
- Record consent (`POST /consent` or `service('contacts').grantConsent`) when your app collects it. Sending needs `granted` consent for the channel unless the template category is `AUTHENTICATION` and you pass `transactional: true`.
- Switch on `error.details.code`, never on the message text.
- Listen to the `messagegate.*` events on `strapi.eventHub` instead of polling.

Don't:

- Don't call Meta, Telegram, seven.io or Twilio directly for messages that MessageGate should track; statuses, fallback and consent would be bypassed.
- Don't send the same message again yourself after an `uncertain` status. The provider may have delivered it; MessageGate leaves the decision to an admin.
- Don't use the Content API from a browser or with a users-permissions login. It is for servers with an API token (end users are refused unless `contentApi.allowUsersPermissions` is on).
- Don't put personal data in `metadata` or `tags`. They are stored in plain text and shown to admins.
- Don't expect "online" or "exists on WhatsApp" checks. The official APIs don't offer them (see README, "What the official APIs allow").

## Server API (inside Strapi)

```js
const mg = strapi.plugin('magic-messagegate');

const result = await mg.service('messages').send({
  to: '+4915123456789', // or userId (users-permissions id) or contactId
  channel: 'auto', // 'auto' | 'whatsapp' | 'telegram' | 'sms'
  template: 'order_shipped', // template key
  language: 'de',
  variables: { first_name: 'Anna', order_id: 'A-10423' },
  idempotencyKey: 'order-shipped-A-10423',
  notAfter: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 3600_000),
});
// → { id: 'k3j9…', status: 'queued', channel: 'whatsapp', duplicate: false }
```

| Service    | Method                                       | Returns                                                                       |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `messages` | `send(input, { source? })`                   | `{ id, status, channel, duplicate }`                                          |
| `messages` | `get(id)`                                    | message detail (see below)                                                    |
| `messages` | `list(query)`                                | `{ results, pagination }`                                                     |
| `messages` | `retry(id, { confirmDuplicateRisk? })`       | message detail; `uncertain` messages need `confirmDuplicateRisk: true`        |
| `messages` | `cancel(id)`                                 | message detail (status `discarded`)                                           |
| `contacts` | `upsert(phone, { userId?, locale? })`        | contact DTO (phone masked)                                                    |
| `contacts` | `grantConsent(contactId, channel, source?)`  | `undefined`                                                                   |
| `contacts` | `revokeConsent(contactId, channel, source?)` | `undefined`                                                                   |
| `telegram` | `createLink(contactId, accountId?)`          | `{ url, token, expiresInMinutes: 30 }`, `url` is `https://t.me/<bot>?start=…` |
| `lookup`   | `check(phone)`                               | lookup result (see below)                                                     |

### `send` input

| Field            | Type                                                       | Rules                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `to`             | string                                                     | phone number, parsed to E.164 with the default country (`DE`); 3–40 chars |
| `userId`         | integer                                                    | alternative to `to`: users-permissions user linked to a contact           |
| `contactId`      | string                                                     | alternative to `to`                                                       |
| `email`          | string                                                     | used only by the e-mail fallback (Magic Mail)                             |
| `channel`        | `auto` \| `whatsapp` \| `telegram` \| `sms`                | default `auto` = routing rules, then the default chain (`whatsapp → sms`) |
| `template`       | string `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,119}$`                           | template key; `template` or `text` is required                            |
| `language`       | string, e.g. `de`, `pt_BR`                                 | picks the template variant                                                |
| `variables`      | object, ≤ 50 keys, values string ≤ 1024 / number / boolean | validated against the template's variable definitions                     |
| `text`           | string 1–4096                                              | free text (WhatsApp only inside the 24-hour window)                       |
| `idempotencyKey` | string 1–200                                               | scoped per caller (API token or service)                                  |
| `notAfter`       | Date, ISO string with offset, or epoch ms                  | final deadline; default `defaultNotAfterHours` (24)                       |
| `transactional`  | boolean                                                    | with an `AUTHENTICATION` template: no consent needed                      |
| `tags`           | string[] ≤ 10, each ≤ 40                                   | used by routing rules                                                     |
| `accountId`      | string                                                     | send through this account only                                            |
| `priority`       | `high` \| `normal` \| `low`                                | worker order                                                              |
| `metadata`       | object ≤ 20 keys                                           | stored, never sent                                                        |

Unknown fields are rejected (`INVALID_REQUEST`).

### Variables in WhatsApp buttons

- **URL buttons:** Meta lets one variable sit at the **end** of an approved URL, for example `https://shop.example/track/{{order_id}}`. MessageGate sends only the value; WhatsApp appends it to the approved URL. The value must be the URL suffix (`A-10423`), never a full URL. Only the first placeholder of a URL button is used.
- **Copy-code buttons:** set `variable` on the button; the value is cut to 15 characters, Meta's limit.
- Body, header and button variables all come from the same `variables` object.

## Content API (for other services)

Base path `/api/magic-messagegate`. Authenticate with a Strapi API token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) that has the MessageGate permissions. Bodies may be wrapped in `{ "data": … }`.

| Method | Path             | Body                                                        | Success                                                                                                                     |
| ------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/messages`      | `send` input                                                | `202 { data: { id, status, channel, duplicate: false } }`, replay `200 … duplicate: true`                                   |
| GET    | `/messages/:id`  | –                                                           | `200 { data: { id, status, channel, templateKey, errorCode, sentAt, deliveredAt, readAt, failedAt, timeline, fallbacks } }` |
| POST   | `/consent`       | `{ phone, channel, status: 'granted'\|'revoked', userId? }` | `200 { data: { contactId, channel, status } }`                                                                              |
| POST   | `/telegram-link` | `{ phone }`                                                 | `200 { data: { url, token, expiresInMinutes } }`                                                                            |
| POST   | `/lookup`        | `{ phone }`                                                 | `200 { data: lookup result }`                                                                                               |

Rate limits (shared across all processes): `rateLimits.sendPerMinute` (120) per token for `/messages`, `rateLimits.lookupPerMinute` (30) for `/lookup`. Over the limit: `429` with `Retry-After: 60` and code `RATE_LIMITED`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://cms.example.com/api/magic-messagegate/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STRAPI_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data":{"to":"+4915123456789","template":"order_shipped","language":"de","variables":{"first_name":"Anna","order_id":"A-10423"},"idempotencyKey":"order-shipped-A-10423"}}'
```

Errors use Strapi's error shape:

```json
{
  "data": null,
  "error": { "status": 409, "name": "ConflictError", "message": "…", "details": { "code": "NO_CONSENT" } }
}
```

## Message detail and statuses

`timeline` is a list of `{ type, code, at }` (epoch ms), `fallbacks` a list of `{ id, channel, status }` for messages created by the fallback chain.

| Status      | Meaning                                                                                    | Terminal |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| `queued`    | waiting for the worker (also between retries)                                              | no       |
| `sent`      | the provider accepted it                                                                   | no       |
| `delivered` | the provider reported delivery to the phone                                                | no       |
| `read`      | the recipient opened it (WhatsApp only, and only with read receipts on)                    | yes      |
| `failed`    | not delivered (`errorCode`, e.g. `META_131026`); the fallback chain may continue           | yes      |
| `uncertain` | the outcome is unknown (timeout after the request was written); never resent automatically | yes      |
| `expired`   | `notAfter` passed before it could be sent                                                  | yes      |
| `discarded` | cancelled by an admin or `cancel(id)`                                                      | yes      |

Statuses only move forward: a late `delivered` after `read` is ignored. Retries: first try plus up to 3 retries after about 1, 5 and 15 minutes (±20 %), only when the provider provably did not accept the message.

## Lookup result

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "e164": "+4915123456789",
  "country": "DE",
  "type": "MOBILE",
  "mobile": true,
  "whatsapp": "unknown",
  "remote": null
}
```

`whatsapp` is `unknown`, `ok` (a message was delivered) or `unreachable` (Meta reported 131026). `remote` holds the cached Twilio line-type result when paid lookups are enabled, otherwise `null`.

## Events (`strapi.eventHub`)

No phone numbers, names or message text in any payload.

| Event                                 | Payload                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `messagegate.message.queued`          | `{ messageId, channel, templateKey, status, code?, at }`                                       |
| `messagegate.message.sent`            | same                                                                                           |
| `messagegate.message.delivered`       | same                                                                                           |
| `messagegate.message.read`            | same                                                                                           |
| `messagegate.message.failed`          | same, `code` set                                                                               |
| `messagegate.message.uncertain`       | same, `code` set                                                                               |
| `messagegate.message.expired`         | same, `code: 'DEADLINE_PASSED'`                                                                |
| `messagegate.message.discarded`       | same                                                                                           |
| `messagegate.message.fallback`        | `{ messageId, channel, templateKey, status: 'fallback', code, at }` (`channel` = next channel) |
| `messagegate.contact.opted-out`       | `{ channel, at }`                                                                              |
| `messagegate.contact.unreachable`     | `{ channel: 'whatsapp', at }`                                                                  |
| `messagegate.template.status-changed` | template id, key, language, new status                                                         |

```js
strapi.eventHub.on('messagegate.message.read', ({ messageId, templateKey }) => {
  /* … */
});
```

## Error codes

| Code                       | HTTP | When                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `INVALID_REQUEST`          | 400  | body does not match the schema                                               |
| `INVALID_PHONE`            | 400  | not a valid mobile number                                                    |
| `MISSING_VARIABLE`         | 400  | a required template variable is missing (`details.field`)                    |
| `INVALID_VARIABLE`         | 400  | a variable is too long or unknown, or the rendered Telegram text is too long |
| `CONFIG_INVALID`           | 400  | account or settings configuration is invalid                                 |
| `INVALID_SIGNATURE`        | 401  | webhook signature check failed                                               |
| `FORBIDDEN`                | 403  | Content API without an API token, or a paid lookup without `contacts.manage` |
| `NOT_FOUND`                | 404  | unknown message, contact, template or account                                |
| `UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`         | 404  | no active template with this key for the channel                             |
| `TEMPLATE_NOT_APPROVED`    | 409  | WhatsApp template not approved by Meta yet                                   |
| `NO_CONSENT`               | 409  | no granted consent for the channel                                           |
| `SUPPRESSED`               | 409  | contact suppressed (opted out, blocked the bot, not on WhatsApp)             |
| `WINDOW_CLOSED`            | 409  | free text outside the 24-hour WhatsApp window                                |
| `NO_ACCOUNT`               | 409  | no active account for the channel                                            |
| `NO_ROUTE`                 | 409  | no channel in the chain can reach the contact                                |
| `NOT_LINKED`               | 409  | contact has not linked Telegram                                              |
| `DEADLINE_PASSED`          | 409  | `notAfter` has passed                                                        |
| `STATE_CHANGED`            | 409  | the message changed meanwhile (retry/discard race)                           |
| `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`    | 409  | retrying an `uncertain` message without `confirmDuplicateRisk`               |
| `PAYLOAD_PURGED`           | 409  | the message content was already removed by retention                         |
| `LOOKUP_DISABLED`          | 409  | paid lookup not configured                                                   |
| `EMBEDDED_SIGNUP_DISABLED` | 409  | Meta Embedded Signup not configured on the server                            |
| `RATE_LIMITED`             | 429  | too many requests                                                            |
| `LOOKUP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`   | 429  | monthly lookup budget used up                                                |
| `PROVIDER_ERROR`           | 502  | the provider rejected an admin action (template submit, account test)        |

Provider error codes in `errorCode` and timelines are prefixed: `META_131026`, `TG_403`, `SEVEN_…`, `TWILIO_…`, plus `TIMEOUT`, `LEASE_EXPIRED_DURING_SEND`, `DEADLINE_PASSED`.

## Webhooks (configured by the owner, not called by apps)

`GET|POST /api/magic-messagegate/webhooks/:provider/:path`, where `:path` is a random id per account shown in the admin (Meta app-level URL: `/webhooks/meta/app`). Every POST must carry the provider signature (`X-Hub-Signature-256`, `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`, seven.io `X-Signature`, `X-Twilio-Signature`); otherwise `401` without detail. Events are deduplicated, and Meta retries for up to 36 hours.
